records.label: Example
records.quote: The following frequency distribution shows the marks of 40 students in an exam
records.stem: The following frequency distribution shows the marks of 40 students in an exam (table). Find the standard deviation for this distribution.
solution: 1: Find the centers of sets x. Then: The center of the first set = (0+4)/2 = 2; the center of the second set = (4+8)/2 = 6; and then record them in the third column.
2: Multiply the centers of sets × its corresponding frequencies: i.e. x × k and record in the fourth column. Then find the mean $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum xk}{\sum k}$
3: Find the deviation of the center of each set (x) from the mean i.e. find $(x - \bar{x})$
4: Find squares of deviations of the center of each set from the mean: i.e $(x-\bar{x})^2$
5: Find the product of the square deviation of the center of each set from the mean × frequency of this set; i.e. $(x-\bar{x})^2 \times k$
6: Calculate the standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (x-\bar{x})^2 k}{\sum k}}$
records.notes: Example is unnumbered; solution gives method steps only, no final answer on this page; continues on next page presumably.

records.notes: Total row's first cell printed 'Sets' (likely meant Total). Overbars on x read from image.

records.text: The mean $\bar{x} = \frac{504}{40} = 12.6$

records.quote: The standard deviation σ = √(817.6/40) = √20.44 ≃ 4.52 marks
records.text: The standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{817.6}{40}} = \sqrt{20.44} \simeq 4.52$ marks
